specName: Companion steps read spec-kit's template stack

FR-001.title: The build reads spec, plan and tasks templates through spec-kit's resolver

FR-002.title: Configured section swaps apply to the resolved template

FR-003.title: An override or preset with nothing configured is written and followed whole

FR-004.title: No customisation means no copy and byte-identical bodies

FR-005.title: The built copy lives in a project-owned folder

FR-006.title: No resolver script falls back to the core template

FR-007.title: A resolver failure stops the build before writing

FR-008.title: The doctor reports a missing or stale built copy for an override or preset

decisions.decision: call spec-kit resolve-template.sh from the build
decisions.why: Companion then agrees with stock runs as the stack order and preset composition change
decisions.rejected: a Python port of the lookup order

decisions.decision: no script or no bash falls back to core; a script that fails stops the build
decisions.why: old installs keep working, real mismatches surface

decisions.decision: ignore Companion's own old extension-layer copy and delete it after a successful write
decisions.why: spec-kit ranks it above core, so a new build would read its own stale output
decisions.rejected: deleting before resolving, which breaks write-nothing-on-failure

decisions.why: template is taken by the tasks.md shape check

decisions.decision: the doctor judges team templates by file layout and modified times, not by calling the resolver
decisions.why: the doctor ships in the spec-kit extension and the template code and build do not; importing them broke the packaging gate
decisions.rejected: importing template_render and build-pipeline into the doctor, or shipping them

decisions.decision: BUILT_TEMPLATES_REL and STEP_TEMPLATES live in spec_context.py
decisions.why: the shipped doctor and the build-only template code need one owner for the path and names
decisions.rejected: a second copy of the path in the doctor

decisions.decision: a resolver failure with no core template returns no template
decisions.why: the real resolver exits 1 when no layer has the file, which is not a broken stack
decisions.rejected: raising, which broke every project missing a core template

plan.summary: base_template() in template_render.py asks spec-kit which template wins; build, panel, settings writer and doctor share it
plan.key_finding: Companion's old built copy is itself an extension layer, so the first new build would otherwise read its own stale output

implement.summary: The build, panel and settings writer read templates through spec-kit's stack; copies live in .specify/companion/built; the doctor names a team template Companion has not caught up with

approach: One function, base_template(), runs spec-kit's resolve-template.sh and is the only way any script reads a base template. The build swaps sections on top of it, writes an override or preset whole when nothing is configured, and writes every copy to .specify/companion/built/. A new doctor check, built, compares that copy with what the build would write now.

concerns.note: The doctor flags a stale copy by modified time, so a template touched without a content change reads as stale until the next build.
The doctor does not see a configured section swap whose copy is missing; only overrides and presets.
